newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan SESC proposes Finance Ministry punish Nomura.
newsitem.headline: Japan SESC proposes Finance Ministry punish Nomura.

text.p: Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC), said on Tuesday that it has recommended that the Ministry of Finance punish Nomura Securities Co Ltd for violating the Securities and Exchange Law.

The SESC said in a statement that it recommended the administrative punishment because the company and four of its officials, including a former president, apparently violated Japan's securities law by compensating clients for investment losses.

Nomura contributed around 47.5 million yen worth of profits earned from discretionary deals to a client over the January to June period in 1995, which involved transferring money on five occasions from a Nomura account to the corporate client's account, it said.
In March 1995, Nomura paid about 2.2 million yen of profits raised through warrant trading to the client, it said.
The SESC also said that in March 1995, Nomura made a payoff of 320 million yen in cash to the client.

An SESC official told reporters that the watchdog also recommended that the finance minister take appropriate measures to improve Nomura's internal risk control system to avoid any recurrence of the activities.

The illegal compensation for the client happened even though the top brokerage established a system to prevent such illegal deals after it was involved in a client loss compensation scandal in 1991, he said.
